title: Multi-home multipath steering and soft-pin jitter for capacity-aware failover
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We need a routing policy that tolerates transient regional capacity pressure without large SLO regressions or hard traffic shifts. Existing hard geo-pinning or immediate hedging causes oscillations and poor cache utilization. Goal: introduce 'multi-home multipath steering' with soft-pin jitter and a burst-aware circuit breaker so requests can be steered across multiple candidate regions simultaneously while preserving locality, KV cache hit-rates, and SLOs. This ticket covers design, simulation, Canary rollout, and console telemetry work.
acceptance_criteria: A/B test shows <=5% p95 latency increase for pinned customers under 20% global traffic surge compared to baseline
Region-level soft-pin jitter prevents >10% of traffic reflows in the first 60s after capacity change
Circuit breaker rejects requests above budget and exposes clear rationale in traces and Console (reason=burst-budget-exhausted or reason=latency-degrade)
Dashboards show per-model SLO burn rate and multipath allocation distribution
End-to-end canary (10% traffic) stable for 48h with rollback playbook verified
tasks: Design multipath allocation algorithm (weighting by latency, capacity headroom, kv-cache-hit penalty)
Implement soft-pin jitter scheduler in steering service
Add burst-token bucket circuit breaker in request director
Integrate headers and span tags for reason codes and multipath decisions
Create Console widgets: multipath map, per-region capacity credit, and SLO alignment view
Write simulation harness and run deterministic surge tests
Prepare canary rollout plan and runbook
Add e2e tests and unit tests for allocation/CB logic
design_notes: Core idea: each request gets a ranked candidate list (primary, secondary, tertiary). The director computes a multipath weight vector W based on: recent p50/p95 latency delta, available capacity credits, kv cache affinity penalty, and customer pin weight.
Soft-pin jitter: when customer's pin weight > 0.7, apply a small stochastic jitter window (0-12s) that staggers re-routing to avoid thundering herd when a region changes state.

Burst-aware CB: maintain rate-limited token buckets per region-model pair; tokens are consumed by forwarded requests. When exhausted, director will reduce weights to that region and tag traces with reason=budget-exhausted. Token refill rates tied to autoscaler metrics and projected capacity.

SLO coupling: steering decisions must be aware of both latency SLO (p95 target per customer) and an optional cost SLO (maximize lower-cost regions subject to latency constraints). The allocation function supports an alpha parameter to prioritize cost vs latency.

Fallback semantics: maintain deterministic fallback order; multipath is used primarily for hedging and graceful degradation. When region is fully down, fallback to fallback list with circuit-breaker gating.
test_plan: Unit tests covering weight vector math and jitter window behavior
Simulation: synthetic workload with heartbeat capacity drops to verify transient behavior; run 1000 deterministic seeds
Chaos test: kill a region VM pool and ensure staggered reflow across clients (no >15% immediate reflow to a single target)
Canary: 10% of production traffic for initial 48 hours with elevated logging and automatic rollback if p95 increases >10%
Load test: sustained 30% traffic surge for 1 hour with metrics tracked for redispatch rate, kv cache hit-rate, and cost delta
rollout_plan: Merge feature flag guarded code behind ff:multihome_multipath
Stage 2: 1% production traffic with elevated tracing for 24h
Stage 4: 50% if stable for 72h, monitor burn rates, then 100%
Rollback: automatic if p95 > 20% or error rate increase > 2x ; manual rollback playbook documented in links
metrics: per-customer p95 latency (target <= 300ms for tier-1 under normal load)
region allocation entropy (lower bound to preserve cache locality)
SLO burn rate and error budget remaining
risks: Overly aggressive multipath allocation may reduce KV cache hit rate leading to cost and latency regressions
Jitter window tuning mistakes could cause long tails if too large or unnecessary oscillation if too small
Incorrect token bucket sizing may cause excessive rejects during short surges; ties to autoscaler must be reliable
Instrumentation gaps could make root cause analysis difficult — we must ensure reason codes are present in traces and logs
